case_title.quote: KUNJUMON @ UNNI v. STATE OF KERALA
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment caption.

number_of_accused.quote: The appellant along with another accused 'JJ' was prosecuted
number_of_accused.reason: Two accused: the appellant and Jose Joseph (JJ).

accused_gender.reason: Appellant is referred to as male ('he', 'his client').

accused_age.reason: The judgment gives no age for the appellant.

accused_religion.reason: Religion of the accused is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_caste.reason: Caste of the accused is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_occupation.reason: Occupation of the accused is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Socioeconomic status of the accused is not mentioned in the judgment.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No previous criminal record is mentioned in the judgment.

victim_gender.quote: attempted to rob Lidiya's grandmother Annamma, aged about 90 years of her ornaments
victim_gender.reason: Victim Annamma is a woman, referred to as 'her'.

victim_caste.reason: Victim's caste is not mentioned in the judgment.

victim_religion.reason: Victim's religion is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_victim_relationship.correct_value: Stranger to PW-2 Lidiya; accused's relationship to Annamma is not stated
accused_victim_relationship.quote: since he was a total stranger to Lidiya
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Stranger status is stated only regarding Lidiya, not the victim Annamma.

offence_category.reason: Principal conviction is murder under s.302, alongside robbery.

statutory_provisions.correct_value: IPC ss.302, 397, 449 (charged); s.449 conviction set aside; s.34 not mentioned
statutory_provisions.quote: charged with offences punishable under Section 449 of the IPC, Section 397 of the IPC and Section 302 of the IPC
statutory_provisions.reason: Omits that s.449 was set aside; s.34 is never cited in the judgment.

weapon.quote: beat her on the head with a wall clock

evidence_type.quote: The Trial Judge found from the medical evidence given by PW-10 Dr. V.P. Rajan
evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness, medical and recovery evidence all relied upon.

confession.reason: No confession is mentioned; 'None' asserts an absence the judgment does not address.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: If a frail old woman aged about 90 years is dragged down from her cot and beaten on the head with a wall clock
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Court relied on the frail age, the wall clock and the resulting death.

mitigating_circumstances.correct_value: Court rejected claim of no intent to kill; accused entered to rob, not to kill (para 32)
mitigating_circumstances.quote: There is no merit in the submission of learned counsel for the appellant that his client did not intend the death of Annamma
mitigating_circumstances.reason: Value says appellant did not intend to kill, which the court expressly rejected.

trial_court_outcome.quote: the Trial Court convicted the appellant and sentenced him to 10 years imprisonment
trial_court_outcome.reason: Trial court convicted under ss.449, 397 and 302.

high_court_outcome.correct_value: High Court rejected the appeal and upheld conviction and sentence under ss.449, 397 and 302
high_court_outcome.quote: the High Court rejected the appeal and upheld the conviction of the appellant
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court did not acquit under s.449; it upheld the conviction entirely.

final_outcome.correct_value: Convicted under ss.302 and 397; acquitted under s.449; appeal partly allowed
final_outcome.quote: the appeal is allowed to the extent that no offence punishable under Section 449 of the IPC has been made out
final_outcome.reason: 'Convicted' omits the partial acquittal under s.449 by the Supreme Court.

offence_finally_established.correct_value: Murder (s.302) and robbery with attempt to cause death (s.397); s.449 not established
offence_finally_established.quote: Section 397 (robbery or dacoity, with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt)
offence_finally_established.reason: Grievous hurt is not a finding; s.449 omitted from the established offences.

imprisonment_type.quote: and for life for an offence punishable under Section 302 of the IPC

imprisonment_years.quote: and for life for an offence punishable under Section 302
imprisonment_years.reason: Life term carries no years figure, so null is appropriate.

fine_rs.quote: sentenced him to 10 years imprisonment and fine
fine_rs.reason: Fine is mentioned but no amount is stated, so null is correct.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Trial court convicted under ss.302, 397 and 449 IPC; High Court dismissed appeal; victim is PW-2's grandmother, not daughter
neutral_facts.quote: The High Court rejected the appeal and upheld the conviction of the appellant
neutral_facts.reason: Wrongly says victim's daughter was the witness, trial convictions were misstated, and HC acquitted under s.449.

offence_severity.correct_value: s.302 life imprisonment; s.397 seven years imprisonment (trial court); no maximum stated
offence_severity.quote: imprisonment for 7 years and fine for an offence punishable under Section 397
offence_severity.reason: Seven years for s.397 is stated; the life maximum for s.397 is not in the judgment.

attempt_completion.quote: robbed her of her gold chain weighing about 5.500 grams

physical_harm.quote: causing injuries on head of a lady of 90 years, which resulted in her death
physical_harm.reason: Head injuries causing death of a 90-year-old are stated.

number_of_offences.quote: charged with offences punishable under Section 449 of the IPC, Section 397 of the IPC and Section 302
number_of_offences.reason: Three charges; ss.302 and 397 upheld, s.449 not made out.

financial_property_loss.correct_value: Gold chain (about 5.500 grams), two gold ear studs and two imitation bangles taken; gold ornaments recovered
financial_property_loss.quote: weighing about 5.500 grams by breaking it from her neck
financial_property_loss.reason: Property was taken and partly recovered; 'Not applicable' is wrong.

premeditation_planning.correct_value: Entry was for robbery with common intention; court found no intention to kill anybody
premeditation_planning.quote: He did not go for the purpose of or with the intention to kill anybody
premeditation_planning.reason: Robbery planning is supported; 'premeditation for murder' is an inference the judgment does not state.

motive.quote: with the common intention of committing robbery

key_evidence_accepted.quote: the injuries could have been caused by a wall clock as alleged by the prosecution
key_evidence_accepted.reason: PW-2 evidence, medical evidence and recovery were relied upon.

witness_credibility.quote: must be placed, in our opinion, on a somewhat higher pedestal, in terms of the credibility attached to it
witness_credibility.reason: Matches the court's higher-credibility reasoning for victim PW-2.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Recovery of stolen gold ornaments at appellant's instance on 24 October 1997
post_offence_conduct.quote: the Investigating Officer PW-13 T.A. Salim recovered the stolen articles at the instance of the appellant
post_offence_conduct.reason: Post-offence recovery at accused's instance is stated, so 'Not stated' is incomplete.

custody_duration.reason: Custody duration is not mentioned in the judgment.

bail_history.reason: Bail history is not mentioned in the judgment.

trial_duration.quote: On 20th October 1997, the appellant and Jose Joseph came
trial_duration.reason: Offence date, HC and SC dates stated; trial judgment date not stated.

legal_representation.quote: Purnima Bhar for the Appellant. Liz Mathew, Sana Hasmi for the Respondent.

investigation_status.correct_value: Complaint lodged; investigation concluded; challan filed; trial completed
investigation_status.quote: On a complaint having been lodged of the robbery, the police investigated the case
investigation_status.reason: FIR registration is not stated; complaint, challan and trial are.

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: No TIP conducted; trial judge's cursory treatment of identification; six-year delay in recording child witness
procedural_irregularity.quote: the unfortunately cursory manner in which the matter has been dealt with by the Trial Judge and the High Court
procedural_irregularity.reason: Judgment notes cursory treatment, absence of TIP and six-year evidence delay.

appeal_history.quote: the appeal is allowed to the extent that no offence punishable under Section 449
appeal_history.reason: Trial conviction, HC upheld, SC partly allowed matches the record.

prosecution_argument.quote: this was also the case of the prosecution, that the appellant had gone to the house of Jose son of Anthony for the purpose of committing a robbery
prosecution_argument.reason: Prosecution case on robbery purpose and the assault is supported.

defence_argument.correct_value: Defence also argued child witness evidence should be carefully scrutinized, besides TIP and no intent to murder
defence_argument.quote: the evidence of the child witness should be carefully scrutinized
defence_argument.reason: Omits the child-witness scrutiny argument; 'victim unreliable' is loosely worded.

legal_principle_applied.quote: The sum and substance of the various decisions referred to above
legal_principle_applied.reason: Failure to hold TIP not fatal; circumspection on stranger identification; victimology stated.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Sk. Hasib v. State of Bihar, AIR 1972 SC 283 cited para 15
precedent_relied_upon.reason: All listed precedents appear in the judgment's references.

sentencing_rationale.correct_value: Convictions under ss.302 and 397 upheld as correct; s.449 not made out as house trespass was for robbery, not murder
sentencing_rationale.quote: it would not be proper to convict the appellant for an offence punishable under Section 449 of the IPC
sentencing_rationale.reason: Captures the s.449 reasoning but the judgment gives no sentencing rationale as such.

judicial_mitigating_factors.correct_value: Accused went to house to rob, not to kill, leading to s.449 acquittal
judicial_mitigating_factors.quote: He did not go for the purpose of or with the intention to kill anybody
judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: 'None' ignores the court's no-intent-to-kill reasoning behind the s.449 acquittal.

judicial_aggravating_factors.correct_value: Frail 90-year-old victim dragged from cot and beaten on head with wall clock
judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: If a frail old woman aged about 90 years is dragged down from her cot and beaten on the head with a wall clock
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Court relied on the victim's frailty and the assault as grounds for murder.

other_sentence_order.correct_value: Trial court directed that sentences run concurrently
other_sentence_order.quote: It was directed that the sentences would run concurrently.
other_sentence_order.reason: Concurrent sentencing order is stated in the judgment.
